{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Re-read the data with explicit dtype for revenue to object
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv', dtype={'revenue': 'object'})

# Verify all premises
assert 'loyal' in df['customer_segment'].unique(), "'loyal' segment not found in data"
assert len(df['customer_segment'].unique()) == 3, "Expected exactly 3 customer_segment values"
assert 'completed' in df['status'].unique(), "'completed' status not found in data"
assert (df['revenue'] == '999999.99').sum() == 0, "QA rows with revenue '999999.99' exist in data, but should not"
assert df['revenue'].dtype == 'object', "Revenue must be object dtype"
assert (df['status'] == 'refunded').sum() > 0, "Refunded orders should exist in data"

# Convert revenue: remove commas and cast to float
df['revenue_float'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Filter for loyal customers and completed orders
loyal_completed = df[
    (df['customer_segment'] == 'loyal') & 
    (df['status'] == 'completed')
]

# Check for QA rows in loyal_completed
qa_check = (loyal_completed['revenue_float'] == 999999.99).sum()
print(f'QA rows in loyal_completed: {qa_check}')

# Remove QA rows if any (even if doc says 0, verify)
loyal_completed_clean = loyal_completed[loyal_completed['revenue_float'] != 999999.99]

# Compute mean revenue
mean_revenue = loyal_completed_clean['revenue_float'].mean()

# Print the key numbers explicitly
print(f'Number of loyal completed orders (after QA removal): {len(loyal_completed_clean)}')
print(f'Mean revenue: {mean_revenue}')

# Return the mean_revenue
mean_revenue"}
